answer.answer: U.S. export controls have effectively foreclosed NVIDIA from China's data center compute market as of the end of fiscal year 2026, because it cannot create a competitive product that both the USG and the Chinese government approve [1]. The company says this foreclosure helped competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge it worldwide [1]. A new H200 licensing program requires a U.S. inspection before shipment, so any H200 shipped under it will face a 25% tariff on import into the United States, which NVIDIA may not be able to pass on to customers [1]. The controls also left NVIDIA with excess inventory and purchase obligations on the H20 [2]. Chinese regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls, which required offering degraded products to China, violated the terms of China's Mellanox approval [3]. The Chinese government has also encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged them from buying NVIDIA data center products, including China-specific products designed to comply with U.S. controls [4].

answer.answer: On September 8, 2025, PTFI experienced an external mud rush incident that resulted in seven fatalities [1]. Approximately 800,000 metric tons of wet material entered the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine from the former Grasberg open pit and traveled rapidly to multiple levels of the mine, including a service level where seven team members were later found deceased [2]. Mining operations were temporarily suspended to prioritize the recovery of the seven team members and to conduct investigations [1]. In late October 2025, PTFI restarted operations at the unaffected Deep Mill Level Zone (DMLZ) and Big Gossan underground mines [2]. Investigations and remedial plans were completed in fourth-quarter 2025, and a phased restart and ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine is anticipated to begin in second-quarter 2026 [1]. Smelting operations at both PTFI's smelter and PT Smelting were temporarily suspended during fourth-quarter 2025 as a result of limited copper concentrate availability [3].
